# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 65 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 65 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_065_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 6, Part 3 — The Purpose of the Angel of Punishment

**65:1** "Now here is how the angel of punishment works — the one to whom people who fall away from God are handed over. He afflicts each person in proportion to what they deserve based on their deeds. Those who have sinned greatly receive many torments; those who have sinned less receive fewer."

**65:2** "But how exactly does the angel of punishment afflict a sinful person?" "Through every kind of suffering they are deserving of in their life," he said — "various losses: loss of money, loss of possessions. Various illnesses and severe afflictions. All kinds of adversity. These things are the source of sufferings, diseases, and various troubles."

**65:3** "But none of these things," he said, "come from any hatred or malice toward the person. They come because God wants to save them. Because God loves them, God hastens to discipline them — so that this person can be purified from the deep iniquity that is in them."

**65:4** "Those who are God's servants and carry God within their hearts — when they realize they are being afflicted in some way, they think back on their sins and evil deeds and repent. After repenting, they live for God for the rest of their days."

**65:5** "But a person who has nothing within themselves to resist the angel of punishment — they remain under his torments until their days are ended."

---

*PNEUMA renders for contemporary clarity and accessibility, capturing the corrective-remedial purpose of the angel of punishment in Hermas's theology.*
